stem: Which of these is a direct tax?

options.content: Corporate tax on company profits
options.rationale: Correct: charged on profit and paid directly by the company.

options.content: Value added tax
options.rationale: VAT is charged on spending: an indirect tax.

options.content: Customs duty on imports
options.rationale: Duties on goods are indirect taxes.

options.content: Excise duty on fuel and cigarettes
options.rationale: Excise duty is charged on goods: indirect.

explanation: Direct taxes fall on income, profit or wealth; corporate tax is one.

stem: Which body collects taxes and customs duties in Zimbabwe?

options.content: The Zimbabwe Revenue Authority
options.rationale: Correct: ZIMRA assesses and collects taxes and duties.

options.content: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
options.rationale: The central bank manages money and banks, not tax collection.

options.content: The Consumer Council of Zimbabwe
options.rationale: It protects consumers.

options.content: The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange
options.rationale: It is a market for shares.

explanation: ZIMRA is responsible for collecting revenue for the government.

stem: Why is VAT described as an indirect tax?

options.content: It is charged only on company profits
options.rationale: That describes corporate tax.

options.content: It is collected by sellers and passed on in prices
options.rationale: Correct: consumers pay it through the price, not directly.

options.content: It is paid only by people with high incomes
options.rationale: Everyone who buys taxed goods pays VAT.

options.content: It is deducted from wages by employers
options.rationale: That describes income tax deducted at source.

explanation: Indirect taxes are on spending; the seller collects and pays them over.

stem: Which canon of taxation is met when income tax is deducted from wages each payday?

options.content: Flexibility
options.rationale: Flexibility is about changing rates when needed.

options.content: Equity
options.rationale: Equity is about fairness and ability to pay.

options.content: Convenience
options.rationale: Correct: it is collected at a convenient time for the taxpayer.

options.content: Economy
options.rationale: Economy is about a low cost of collection.

explanation: Deduction at source collects tax when the worker has the money: convenience.

stem: A government raises the excise duty on cigarettes. What is the **most** likely main aim?

options.content: To protect local cigarette factories from imports
options.rationale: Excise duty falls on local goods too; customs duty protects.

options.content: To reduce the cost of collecting taxes
options.rationale: The duty change does not affect collection cost.

options.content: To make the tax system more progressive
options.rationale: Duties on cigarettes take a larger share from poorer smokers.

options.content: To reduce consumption of a harmful product
options.rationale: Correct: higher prices discourage smoking.

explanation: Taxes on harmful goods raise their price and discourage use, as well as raising revenue.
hints: Excise duty falls on goods made locally as well as imports.

stem: Why are indirect taxes said to be regressive?

options.content: They are charged at higher rates on higher incomes
options.rationale: That describes a progressive tax.

options.content: They reduce the profits of large companies
options.rationale: That is not what regressive means.

options.content: Poor people pay a larger share of their income in them
options.rationale: Correct: everyone pays the same tax on a product whatever their income.

options.content: They are collected only once a year
options.rationale: Indirect taxes are collected whenever goods are bought.

explanation: Equal tax on a loaf takes a bigger fraction of a low income than of a high income.
hints: Compare the tax on one loaf of bread with two different incomes.

stem: Which is a function of ZIMRA at border posts?

options.content: Issuing bank notes and coins
options.rationale: That is the central bank's role.

options.content: Preventing smuggling and collecting customs duty
options.rationale: Correct: ZIMRA controls goods crossing borders.

options.content: Fixing the prices of goods in shops
options.rationale: ZIMRA does not set retail prices.

options.content: Insuring imported goods against loss while in transit
options.rationale: Insurance companies do this.

explanation: At borders ZIMRA checks declarations, collects duty and prevents smuggling.

stem: A solar panel costs US\$380 before VAT. Assume a VAT rate of 15%. Calculate the price including VAT.
Tendai earns US\$850 a month. Assume the first US\$150 is tax-free and the rest is taxed at 25%. Calculate his monthly income tax.
hints: Take off the tax-free amount first.
Apply the rate only to taxable income.

stem: A trader imports goods valued at US\$3,600. Assume customs duty of 40% of the value. How much duty is payable?
Customs duty is charged on goods imported into a country.
explanation: True. Customs duty is an indirect tax on imports (and sometimes exports).

stem: Paying tax is voluntary for small businesses that make little profit.
explanation: False. Paying tax due is a legal obligation; businesses must register, keep records and file returns.

stem: Match each tax with what it is charged on.

right.content: Spending on most goods and services
Certain locally produced goods such as fuel and alcohol
Wages, salaries and other personal income

explanation: Direct taxes are on income and profit; indirect taxes are on spending and goods.

payload.template: A tax on income, profit or wealth is a {{blank:a}} tax. Illegally hiding income to avoid tax is called tax {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Direct taxes fall on income, profit and wealth. Tax evasion is illegal non-payment.

stem: Write the abbreviation of the authority that collects taxes in Zimbabwe.
Explain **two** reasons why a government collects taxes.

points.description: Revenue for public services (1)
Developed, e.g. pays for schools, clinics and roads that people could not provide alone (1)
Second reason, e.g. redistribute income / discourage harmful goods / protect local industry / control inflation (1)
Developed, e.g. duty on imports makes them dearer so local firms can compete (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Governments tax to raise revenue for services such as schools, clinics and roads, which individuals could not provide alone. They also tax imports to protect local industries, because customs duty makes imported goods dearer and helps local firms compete.

hints: Think about spending and about influencing behaviour.

stem: Explain **one** advantage and **one** disadvantage of indirect taxes.

points.description: Advantage, e.g. difficult to evade / can target harmful goods / everyone who spends contributes (1)
Explained, e.g. tax is in the price, so it is paid automatically when goods are bought (1)
Disadvantage, e.g. regressive / raises prices / may cause inflation (1)
Explained, e.g. poor households pay a larger share of their income on the same purchases (1)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Indirect taxes are hard to evade because they are part of the price, so anyone who buys goods pays them. However, they are regressive: a poor family pays the same tax on a bag of maize meal as a rich family, which is a larger share of its income.

explanation: Indirect taxes are efficient to collect but fall more heavily on the poor.

stem: Sipho runs a registered furniture workshop in Bulawayo. Assume a VAT rate of 15%. He buys timber for US\$520 plus VAT and sells a wardrobe made from it for US\$1,300 plus VAT. Each month his employees' income tax is deducted from their wages and paid to ZIMRA. A friend suggests he could avoid VAT by selling for cash without receipts.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the VAT Sipho charges on the wardrobe.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: VAT is charged on the value added. Calculate the VAT Sipho pays over to ZIMRA after deducting the VAT he paid on the timber.
parts.explanation: 195 − 78 = US\$117, which is 15% of the value added (780).
parts.workedSolution: 1. 195 − 78 = US\$117, which is 15% of the value added (780).

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Deducting employees' income tax from wages each month meets which canon of taxation?

options.content: Equity
options.rationale: Equity is about ability to pay.

options.content: Flexibility
options.rationale: Flexibility is about changing rates.

options.content: Certainty
options.rationale: Certainty is about knowing what to pay.

options.content: Convenience
options.rationale: Correct: tax is collected when wages are paid.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Discuss whether Sipho should follow his friend's suggestion.

points.description: Not charging VAT due is tax evasion: illegal (1)
Penalties: fines, interest, possible closure or prosecution after a ZIMRA audit (1)
Cash sales without receipts mean poor records; he cannot prove his costs or apply for loans (1)
Reduces revenue for public services / unfair to honest competitors (1)
Justified conclusion: he should not; keep records and pay VAT due (1)

explanation: VAT on the sale US\$195; less VAT on timber US\$78 = US\$117 paid over. Evasion is illegal and risky.
hints: Subtract the VAT already paid on inputs.

stem: Nyasha is a cross-border trader who imports kitchenware from a neighbouring country to sell in Mutare.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **two** taxes or duties that Nyasha's business may have to pay.

points.description: Customs duty on imports (1)
VAT / income tax on profits (1)

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain **three** functions ZIMRA performs when Nyasha crosses the border.

points.description: Checks her declaration of goods and their value (1)
Calculates and collects customs duty / VAT (1)
Searches for and seizes smuggled or prohibited goods (1)

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain how customs duty affects the price Nyasha charges and her customers.

points.description: Duty is added to her cost of goods (1)
She raises her selling price to keep her profit (1)
Customers pay more / may buy local substitutes instead (1)

explanation: Importers pay customs duty and VAT; ZIMRA checks, collects and prevents smuggling; duty raises prices to consumers.
hints: Think about what happens at the border post.
